title: POC weekly ops lifecycle and credentials checkup
next_steps: Redwood to share updated bench spreadsheet with per-model latencies and token costs by EOD 2026-09-18
Customer to confirm KMS key rotation window and provide test key by 2026-09-22
Schedule on-prem validation run with 50k tokens/day profile for week of 2026-09-28
action_items: Avery Chen: upload pilot benchmark spreadsheet and brief commentary - due 2026-09-18
Tom Ruiz: supply service account and KMS test key (or staging creds) - due 2026-09-22
Ravi Kapoor: run trimmed inference smoke test on staging and share logs - due 2026-09-21
header: Date: 2026-09-17 | Time: 15:00 PT | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Avery, Ravi, Samira (Redwood) — Maya, Tom, Elena, Luis, Hannah (BrightLane)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress, credentialing gaps, and environment readiness. Main blockers: KMS key exchange, service account permissions, and an unexpected latency regression in large-batch inference. Agreed actions: share updated benchmark spreadsheet, customer to provide KMS test key, Redwood SE to run focused smoke tests and adjust batching/quant profiles if needed.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: okay everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining, we're on the weekly pilot touchpoint for BrightLane, uh this is Avery from Redwood, i've got Ravi (SE) and Samira (CSM) with me. quick roll call?
[00:12] Maya Patel: hi Maya here, head of platform at BrightLane.
[00:15] Tom Ruiz: Tom — SRE.
[00:17] Elena Watanabe: Elena, CTO.
[00:19] Luis Ortega: Luis, security.
[00:20] Hannah Cho: Hannah, ML eng.
[00:22] Avery Chen: awesome, thanks. i'll kick off with a 2 min status — overall onboarding is at about 75% per our checklist: network peering and firewall rules are in, staging VPC can reach Redwood gateway, but we still need the service account and KMS test key from Tom / Luis to fully validate private key operations.
[00:40] Tom Ruiz: yeah so we've provisioned the SA but we haven't finalized the IAM roles — i'm waiting on details of the exact permissions you need for KV cache and metrics. i can provision a more permissive role for test but would prefer least-priv.
[00:55] Ravi Kapoor: for staging smoke tests we'll need these high-level perms: invoke inference endpoint, read/write to S3-like store for cache artifacts, and list/describe on KMS for decrypt tests. we can also do a mode where KMS operations are mocked if you prefer, but that won't validate rotation semantics.
[01:15] Luis Ortega: rotation semantics is actually a compliance req for us — SOC2-like control. we need to confirm the rotation window, and also audit log integration.
[01:26] Samira Gomez: noted, we have an integration doc (link shared in chat) for KMS/HSM patterns. we'll send an excerpt that maps to BrightLane's controls.
[01:35] Maya Patel: quick operational question — last week's benchmark, we saw a latency spike on larger batch sizes around seq len 1024; is that expected?
[01:45] Ravi Kapoor: good callout. we did observe a regression on the quantized model with aggressive batching — likely kernel selection flipping at that token boundary and more KV cache thrash. i'll own a triage to reproduce and instrument it.
[01:58] Hannah Cho: can you explain 'kernel flipping' in plain terms — is that TPU specific?
[02:04] Ravi Kapoor: sure, tl;dr: different GPU kernels/paths get chosen depending on seq length and batch shape; sometimes the runtime picks a slower path if the pattern crosses a threshold. not TPU, more CUDA/cuBLAS selection behavior mixed with our quant inference path.
[02:20] Elena Watanabe: so does that mean we should avoid larger batch profiles in production?
[02:24] Avery Chen: no, just means we want to tune batch sizes and the quant profile. Redwood Optimize can recommend a sweet spot. for the pilot, Ravi will run focused tests at seq lengths 512, 768, 1024 and share the per-token breakdown.
[02:40] Ravi Kapoor: yup, i'll run those windows. i'm also going to try a 'mixed-kernel' pinning which locks the kernel selection to the fast path for those seq lengths — hoping that reduces the tail latency.
[02:52] Tom Ruiz: sounds good. about KMS — will the test key be a full customer-managed key or can we use a delegated test key?
[03:00] Luis Ortega: i'd prefer CMK for the test to make sure logging and rotation hooks work.
[03:05] Avery Chen: we can do CMK validation; we just need a test key with a short rotation window if you want to verify rotation.
[03:12] Maya Patel: operational priority — we need the on-prem pilot to be as similar to production as possible. we want audit log proof for last 90 days (or an exported slice).
[03:22] Samira Gomez: Redwood supports audit log retention tiers; i'll attach the retention SLAs and the export playbook after the call.
[03:30] Hannah Cho: a quick note from ML — we want to test quality drift after quantization. last week's auto-eval showed a small regression on named-entity recall. has anyone looked at prompt templating changes?
[03:45] Ravi Kapoor: we ran the eval harness with the quant profile, saw a 1.8% drop on NER for our sample prompt set. could be prompt-token alignment differences. i'll coordinate with Hannah to run the same eval offline with a pinned tokenizer version.
[04:00] Hannah Cho: thanks — i'll send the eval set and a baseline run.
[04:05] Elena Watanabe: circling back to latency; if pinning kernels fixes it, what's the cost implication?
[04:12] Ravi Kapoor: good q. pinning to a fast kernel often increases memory utilization a bit, which can reduce packing density — that may raise per-token cost by ~5-12% depending on workload. we should weigh that against SLO needs.
[04:27] Maya Patel: we care about 95th percentile being under 180ms for our chat flow. can Redwood hit that with Dedicated or do we need private?
[04:36] Avery Chen: Hosted + optimized kernels typically hit that for modest concurrency; Dedicated gives more predictable tail but if you need on-prem for data residency that's a separate conversation — for the POC we can validate on staging hosted endpoints first.
[04:50] Tom Ruiz: for compliance we need RBAC over who can call model endpoints and who can retrieve logs. how granular is Redwood's role model?
[04:58] Samira Gomez: we support token-level RBAC, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and per-route role bindings. we'll share a granular RBAC matrix, but short answer — yes, you can control endpoint invocation per service account.
[05:12] Luis Ortega: and the logs — can they be pushed to our SIEM? we prefer pulling via secure export, not storing copies in a third party.
[05:20] Avery Chen: yes, we can ship audit logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export with encryption. we'll include the export pattern in the doc.
[05:28] Maya Patel: okay, nice. let's talk about the staging smoke tests you mentioned. last run had 5k token bursts and we saw an error rate that climbed during sustained bursts.
[05:40] Ravi Kapoor: that was likely kv cache warming and a transient quota on the gateway path. i'll instrument the gateway to expose per-token throttles so we can see where the errors originate.
[05:50] Hannah Cho: are there specific headers we should set to surface trace IDs back to our tracing system?
[05:55] Ravi Kapoor: yes, use x-redwood-trace-id and we will propagate that through our tracing hooks; Samira will share the header doc.
[06:04] Samira Gomez: link: https://redwood.example/pilot-headers (shared in chat).
[06:08] Maya Patel: on the credentials side — i need a clear checklist of the minimal permissions and the sample IAM policy.
[06:15] Avery Chen: understood — we'll attach a minimal IAM policy snippet and a permissive template for smoke tests.
[06:21] Tom Ruiz: timeline-wise, if we provide the KMS key this week, how soon can you run the rotation validation?
[06:27] Ravi Kapoor: if keys arrive by Tuesday we can schedule the rotation test Wed/Thu and share results Fri.
[06:33] Luis Ortega: fine. one more question — is there any PII leakage risk during caching, i.e., do you persist user prompts?
[06:40] Avery Chen: by default Redwood caches prefixes/kv if enabled for cost reduction, but PII can be disabled for the pilot; we also support deterministic redaction policies. we'll default to no-persistence unless you opt in.
[06:54] Hannah Cho: good. can we run a small A/B with caching on/off to measure latency/cost delta?
[06:59] Ravi Kapoor: yes — propose we run a 2-day split: 50% cache on, 50% off, same traffic profile, measure p95 and token cost.
[07:08] Maya Patel: approved. please make sure logs include per-request cache-hit flag.
[07:12] Samira Gomez: we'll include cache-hit metadata in exported logs.
[07:18] Elena Watanabe: any blockers from Redwood side?
[07:21] Avery Chen: only the kernel triage which Ravi will do and upload results; and we need to receive the CMK test key and service account perms.
[07:30] Tom Ruiz: i'll get the SA and KMS key to you by Tuesday.
[07:33] Maya Patel: ditto on the eval set from Hannah.
[07:36] Hannah Cho: sending eval set after this call — expect a gist with 1200 samples.
[07:41] Ravi Kapoor: i'll run the seq length window tests and the cache A/B and post logs to the pilot bucket, plus a short writeup on observed kernel path and mitigation suggestions.
[07:52] Avery Chen: great. a couple administrative things — Samira, can you confirm the billing meter for the pilot? we agreed to credit usage to the trial cap.
[07:59] Samira Gomez: yes, billing is on trial credit; i'll cc finance to confirm.
[08:04] Luis Ortega: security review — i want the SOC2 attestation and penetration test summary.
[08:10] Avery Chen: we have SOC2 Type II and a recent pentest; i'll attach both docs after the call.
[08:16] Maya Patel: fine. before we wrap, let's recap concrete next steps.
[08:20] Avery Chen: recap: 1) Redwood: upload updated benchmark spreadsheet with per-model latency/cost and kernel-triage notes (owner: Avery/Ravi) — due 2026-09-18. 2) BrightLane: provide CMK test key and service account roles (owner: Tom/Luis) — due 2026-09-22. 3) Ravi: run seq length 512/768/1024 triage and cache A/B and post logs/notes (due 2026-09-21). 4) Hannah: share eval set (due 2026-09-18). 5) Samira: share RBAC matrix and log export playbook and confirm billing (due 2026-09-18).
[09:05] Elena Watanabe: okay, thanks. any blockers scheduling the on-prem run the week of Sep 28?
[09:12] Avery Chen: we have capacity; once keys and SA are in we'll schedule the on-prem validation window.
[09:18] Tom Ruiz: noted. thanks everyone.
[09:20] Maya Patel: thanks.
[09:22] [meeting ends]
